title: First Unique Character in a String
notes:
Task: Find the index of the first character appearing exactly once.
Idea: Count every character, then scan the original string from left to right for a count of one.
Invariant: The frequency map is complete before the second scan begins.
Edge cases: If no character is unique, return -1; repeated characters are skipped.
complexity_reason: Two linear scans are used and the counter stores distinct characters.

title: First Unique Character in a String
notes:
Task: Return the first index of a character that appears once, or -1 if none exists.
Idea: Count lowercase letters in a fixed array and scan the string again in order.
Invariant: counts[c] equals the total occurrences of character c in the input.
Edge cases: The fixed array assumes lowercase English letters; a second scan preserves the first unique character's original index.
complexity_reason: Two scans take linear time and the 26-slot array is constant space.

title: Longest Absolute File Path
notes:
Task: Compute the maximum absolute path length to a file described by tab-indented lines.
Idea: Track cumulative directory lengths by depth; a line containing a dot is treated as a file candidate.
Invariant: lengths[d] is the cumulative path length of the directory at depth d, including separators.
Edge cases: No files yields zero; the format uses tabs for nesting and a dot to identify files.
complexity_reason: Each input character is scanned a constant number of times and depth lengths are stored.

title: Longest Absolute File Path
notes:
Task: Find the longest absolute path to a file in a tab-indented file-system description.
Idea: Split into lines, count leading tabs for depth, and maintain cumulative path lengths for directories.
Invariant: lengths[depth] holds the full directory-prefix length before the current name.
Edge cases: File names are identified by a dot as defined by the problem; if no file exists, return zero.
complexity_reason: The input is split and each line is scanned once; the lengths array is linear in line count.

title: Find the Difference
notes:
Task: Find the single extra character in t, which otherwise contains the characters of s shuffled.
Idea: XOR every character code in both strings.
Invariant: Equal character codes cancel in pairs, leaving only the added character code.
Edge cases: The strings differ in length by one; the result is converted back to a character.
complexity_reason: Each character is processed once and only one integer accumulator is stored.

title: Find the Difference
notes:
Task: Return the extra character added to a shuffled copy of s.
Idea: XOR all character codes from both strings so matching characters cancel.
Invariant: The accumulator equals the XOR of all character codes seen so far.
Edge cases: The extra character may occur anywhere; the method does not rely on sorting or order.
complexity_reason: Both strings are scanned once using a single accumulator.

title: Elimination Game
notes:
Task: Find the last remaining number after alternating left-to-right and right-to-left elimination passes.
Idea: Track the first remaining value, gap between survivors, remaining count, and direction.
Invariant: The survivors always form an arithmetic progression with the current head and step.
Edge cases: n=1 returns one; the head advances every pass and on right-to-left passes when count is odd.
complexity_reason: The remaining count is halved each pass.

title: Elimination Game
notes:
Task: Return the final value after repeatedly removing alternating positions from a list 1..n.
Idea: Maintain the first survivor, current step size, count, and elimination direction.
Invariant: The surviving numbers form an arithmetic progression whose step doubles after each round.
Edge cases: n=1 returns 1; the head moves on every left-to-right round and on right-to-left rounds with an odd count.
complexity_reason: Each pass halves remaining and uses a constant number of variables.

title: Is Subsequence
notes:
Task: Determine whether s can be obtained by deleting characters from t without reordering the remaining characters.
Idea: Advance through t and move the s pointer whenever characters match.
Invariant: The matched prefix of s is a subsequence of the already-scanned prefix of t.
Edge cases: Empty s is always a subsequence; if t ends before s is fully matched, return false.
complexity_reason: The method scans t once and stores one pointer into s.

title: Is Subsequence
notes:
Task: Check whether s appears in t in the same character order, with deletions allowed from t.
Idea: Scan t and advance the index into s only when the current characters match.
Invariant: The s prefix already matched can be formed from the scanned t prefix.
Edge cases: An empty s returns true; a nonempty unmatched suffix returns false.
complexity_reason: The two strings are scanned with constant auxiliary state.

title: UTF-8 Validation
notes:
Task: Validate whether each integer represents a byte in a well-formed UTF-8 sequence.
Idea: Determine the expected sequence length from the leading byte, then validate continuation bytes.
Invariant: At the start of each outer iteration, i points to the first byte of the next code point.
Edge cases: Bytes must be in 0..255; continuation bytes must have the high-bit pattern 10.
code:
class Solution:
    def validUtf8(self, data: list[int]) -> bool:
        i=0;n=len(data)
        while i<n:
            x=data[i]
            if x<0 or x>255:return False
            if x>>7==0:count=1
            elif x>>5==0b110:count=2
            elif x>>4==0b1110:count=3
            elif x>>3==0b11110:count=4
            else:return False
            if i+count>n:return False
            for j in range(i+1,i+count):
                if data[j]<0 or data[j]>255 or data[j]>>6!=0b10:return False
            i+=count
        return True
complexity_reason: Every byte is examined once and only counters are stored.

title: UTF-8 Validation
notes:
Task: Determine whether the byte values form valid UTF-8 code points.
Idea: Decode the expected number of bytes from each leading-byte pattern and check each continuation byte.
Invariant: The index advances only by a complete, validated code-point length.
Edge cases: Reject invalid leading patterns, truncated sequences, and continuation bytes that do not start with binary 10.
complexity_reason: The outer index skips complete sequences and each byte is validated once.

title: Decode String
notes:
Task: Decode nested repetition expressions such as k[substring].
Idea: Push the current string and repeat count at each opening bracket; on closing, repeat the inner string and append it to the saved prefix.
Invariant: The stacks preserve the outer context while the current string represents the innermost unfinished segment.
Edge cases: Multi-digit counts are accumulated; input is assumed valid and brackets are balanced.
complexity_reason: Each character is parsed once, while repeated string expansion costs proportional to the decoded output.

title: Decode String
notes:
Task: Expand bracketed strings where each segment is repeated by its preceding integer.
Idea: Store prior prefixes and counts on stacks, then append the repeated inner string when a closing bracket is reached.
Invariant: The current builder contains the decoded content for the innermost open bracket.
Edge cases: Multi-digit repeat counts are parsed digit by digit; the input expression is valid.
complexity_reason: The parser scans input once and the builders store the decoded output.

title: Longest Substring with At Least K Repeating Characters
notes:
Task: Find the longest substring where every character appears at least k times.
Idea: Count characters in the current region; any character occurring fewer than k times splits every valid substring, so recurse on segments between its occurrences.
Invariant: Each recursive call searches only a region that can contain a valid answer.
Edge cases: k<=1 returns the full string length; regions shorter than k cannot qualify.
complexity_reason: Unbalanced splits can rescan overlapping regions across recursion levels.

title: Longest Substring with At Least K Repeating Characters
notes:
Task: Return the longest substring in which each character appears at least k times.
Idea: Count characters in a region and split at any character whose total count is below k.
Invariant: No valid substring can include a character that appears fewer than k times in the current region.
Edge cases: A region shorter than k returns zero; k<=1 allows the full region.
complexity_reason: Repeated substring creation and unbalanced recursive splits can cost quadratic time.

title: Rotate Function
notes:
Task: Maximize the weighted sum across all cyclic rotations of the array.
Idea: Compute F(0) and the array sum, then derive each next rotation's score from the previous score.
Invariant: total is the sum of all values and F(k)=F(k-1)+total-n*A[n-k].
Edge cases: Empty input returns zero; negative values are supported by the recurrence.
complexity_reason: The initial sum is linear and each rotation is updated in constant time.

title: Rotate Function
notes:
Task: Find the maximum weighted sum over all cyclic rotations.
Idea: Calculate the first score and total sum, then update each rotated score with a constant-time recurrence.
Invariant: The rolling value is the score for the current rotation.
Edge cases: An empty array returns zero; the recurrence handles negative array entries.
complexity_reason: The initial pass computes the total and first score; later scores update in constant time.

title: Integer Replacement
notes:
Task: Minimize operations to reduce positive n to one, halving evens and incrementing or decrementing odds.
Idea: For odd values, decrement 3; otherwise increment when the low two bits are 11 and decrement when they are 01.
Invariant: Each operation reduces the integer toward one while favoring an even value with more trailing zeros.
Edge cases: n=1 needs zero operations; use integer arithmetic to avoid floating-point effects.
complexity_reason: Each operation either halves n or changes an odd value to a nearby even value before halving.

title: Integer Replacement
notes:
Task: Find the fewest legal operations to reduce a positive integer to one.
Idea: Halve even values; for odd values, decrement 3 or values ending in binary 01, otherwise increment.
Invariant: The current value remains positive and each chosen odd adjustment enables a subsequent halving.
Edge cases: Use long to safely handle incrementing Integer.MAX_VALUE; n=1 returns zero.
complexity_reason: The greedy process reduces the bit length after at most a constant number of odd adjustments.
